key_insight: Using deployment-specific context (like provider type, department, and model choice) helps predict when clinicians will reject an LLM response better than query content alone.
clinical_relevance: This could enable targeted guardrails or abstention in clinical LLM systems, improving workflow fit by focusing intervention on high-risk interactions.
method: Built a pre-response classifier to estimate rejection risk before generating an answer.
Used query content plus deployment-specific context available in the EHR setting.
Evaluated the model prospectively over 4.5 months of user feedback and assessed two downstream uses: guardrail triggering and abstention.
evidence_signal: In a prospective 4.5-month evaluation, the prediction model achieved AUROC 0.719 for anticipating user rejection.
watch_item: User feedback was sparse and deployment-specific, so performance may not transfer cleanly to other hospitals, departments, or LLM workflows without revalidation.
paper_title: Deployment-Centered Evaluation: Predicting Query-Level Rejection Risk in a Clinical LLM System
